title: Specializing a generic algebraic dependence over a valuation ring
statement: Let $A$ be a valuation ring: an integral domain such that, for $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ and every $x\in K\setminus\{0\}$, either $x\in A$ or $x^{-1}\in A$. Put $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$. Let $B$ be an integral domain containing $A$, let $n\ge0$ be an integer, and let $\alpha:A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\to B$ be an $A$-algebra map [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Put $H=B\otimes_AK$, with the usual tensor algebra multiplication [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and let $L=\operatorname{Frac}(H)$; $H$ is a nonzero domain. If $\operatorname{trdeg}_KL<n$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree], then there is $h\in A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ with $\alpha(h)=0$ and at least one coefficient equal to $1$. For the induced map $\alpha_k:k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\to B\otimes_Ak$, the coefficientwise reduction $\bar h$ of $h$ is nonzero and belongs to $\ker\alpha_k$. No finite type or quasi-finiteness hypothesis on $B$ or on $\alpha$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 00QK (lemma-finite-type-domain-over-valuation-ring-dim-fibres), nonzero generic polynomial kernel and division by a coefficient of minimal valuation, followed by reduction to the residue field.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-generic-fibre-localization-domain-irreducible] to $A\subset B$. Thus $H=B\otimes_AK$ is the nonzero domain obtained by inverting $A\setminus\{0\}$ in $B$ (interchanging tensor factors sends $b\otimes c$ to $c\otimes b$). The map $B\to H\to L$ is injective: $b/1=0$ in the localization means $sb=0$ for some $0\ne s\in A$, hence $b=0$ since $B$ is a domain; the same fraction calculation applies to $H\to\operatorname{Frac}(H)$. Write $y_i$ for the image of $\alpha(t_i)$ in $L$.

source.place: Tag 00QK, lemma-finite-type-domain-over-valuation-ring-dim-fibres, proof: generic kernel, division by a nonzero coefficient of minimal valuation, and reduction modulo the maximal ideal.

proof.text: By [def-kun-transcendence-degree], the inequality $\operatorname{trdeg}_KL<n$ gives a nonzero $f\in K[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ with $f(y_1,\ldots,y_n)=0$. Indeed, if no such relation existed, the $y_i$ would be distinct (otherwise $t_i-t_j$ is a nonzero relation), and the set $\{y_1,\ldots,y_n\}$ would be algebraically independent of cardinality $n$, contrary to the definition of transcendence degree as a supremum. For $n=0$ the hypothesis is impossible, since that supremum is at least $0$. Write $f=\sum_{I\in F}c_It^I$ with $F$ finite nonempty and every $c_I\ne0$, using [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring].

source.place: Tag 00QK, lemma-finite-type-domain-over-valuation-ring-dim-fibres, proof: generic kernel, division by a nonzero coefficient of minimal valuation, and reduction modulo the maximal ideal.

proof.text: For the finite nonempty coefficient list, select a coefficient $c$ such that $c_I/c\in A$ for every $I$. Here is the finite induction directly from the valuation-ring hypothesis: a singleton works; given a selected coefficient $c$ and a new nonzero coefficient $d$, retain $c$ if $d/c\in A$, and otherwise replace it by $d$. In the latter case $c/d\in A$, and every previous ratio $c_I/d=(c_I/c)(c/d)$ lies in $A$. In both cases the selected element remains a coefficient of $f$. Thus $h=\sum_{I\in F}(c_I/c)t^I$ is an element of $A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, and its coefficient at the selected index is exactly $1$.

source.place: Tag 00QK, lemma-finite-type-domain-over-valuation-ring-dim-fibres, proof: generic kernel, division by a nonzero coefficient of minimal valuation, and reduction modulo the maximal ideal.

proof.text: In $L$, evaluation of $h$ at the $y_i$ is $c^{-1}f(y_1,\ldots,y_n)=0$. By the evaluation formula of [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], this is the image of $\alpha(h)\in B$. The injectivity established in step 1 therefore gives $\alpha(h)=0$.

source.place: Tag 00QK, lemma-finite-type-domain-over-valuation-ring-dim-fibres, proof: generic kernel, division by a nonzero coefficient of minimal valuation, and reduction modulo the maximal ideal.

proof.text: Reduce each coefficient of $h=\sum a_It^I$ to $\bar a_I\in k$. Its selected coefficient is $\bar1=1\ne0$, so $\bar h\ne0$ by coefficientwise equality of polynomials [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Put $b_i=\alpha(t_i)$. Bilinearity of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives $\alpha_k(\bar h)=\sum_I(\prod_i b_i^{I_i})\otimes\bar a_I=(\sum_I a_I\prod_i b_i^{I_i})\otimes1=\alpha(h)\otimes1=0$. This also covers $B\otimes_Ak=0$; no injectivity into that ring is used.
